# Willrun

> Willrun answers whether a specific portable power station or generator can run a specific appliance, using published running and starting watts, an 85% inverter allowance for stations, and 30 amp inlet math for home backup.

Willrun is a static site. Every station and appliance row cites a manufacturer or ENERGY STAR URL. Runtime is nameplate watt-hours times 0.85, divided by average draw. The calculator, outage planners, brand comparison, CPAP/BiPAP pages, station and appliance runtime tables, and every station-and-appliance answer page (alongside the simple estimate) also add about 15 W of inverter self-consumption (the figure BLUETTI uses for its AC180) to the draw: Wh × 0.85 ÷ (W + 15). CPAP pages show DC-converter nights separately as a best case. Verdicts are runs, runs with surge risk, won't run, or no run verdict when running watts were not published.

## Start here
- [Calculator](https://willitrunpower.com/): pick a station, add appliances, read the verdict.
- [Methodology](https://willitrunpower.com/methodology/): the 0.85 allowance, duty cycle, and how surge is treated.
- [Stations](https://willitrunpower.com/stations/): 24 models.
- [Appliances](https://willitrunpower.com/appliances/): 40 loads.
- [Affiliate disclosure](https://willitrunpower.com/disclosure/)

Not medical advice.

Penguin II LRA 52-63 A + fan 8.5 A (~7,260-8,580 W on paper), Dometic 3.5 kW min generator; soft starter (EasyStart: 13.5K starts on 2,000 W generator) recommended. A 1,500 W Lasko heater needs at least 1,500 W continuous or a documented resistive boost.
- [Best power station for a sump pump](https://willitrunpower.com/best-power-station-for/sump-pump/): The Zoeller Model 53 at 115 V draws 1,115.5 W while running. Stations under that — including the RIVER 2 series, the AC70, and the Yeti 500X — will not hold it. Stations above it still carry a surge risk because Zoeller does not publish starting amps.

## Outages
- [24-hour outage](https://willitrunpower.com/outage/24-hour/): only the EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 and Anker SOLIX F3800 cover this 24-hour mix once about 15 W of inverter self-consumption is counted (1,608 Wh of appliances + 360 Wh idle = 1,968 Wh, about 2,315 Wh nameplate); the 2 kWh class is about 230 Wh short.
- [3-day power outage backup plan](https://willitrunpower.com/outage/3-day/): A 3-day outage with a full-size fridge, CPAP, router, laptop and lights takes about 6,666 Wh including ~15 W inverter draw (about 7,840 Wh nameplate). Compares battery-only expandable systems (DELTA Pro 3, F3800 Plus, AC200L, Jackery 2000 Plus, DELTA 2 Max), solar with PVWatts monthly sun hours for six cities, and a generator-recharged battery (~1.4 gal over 3 days vs ~8.4 gal running an EU2200i 24/7). CDC CO and FoodSafety.gov guidance, medical note.

# Methodology

## What a verdict means

Runs means the published running watts fit the station's continuous AC output, and any published appliance peak also fits the surge figure Willrun is willing to treat as a motor start.

Runs, surge risk means the running watts fit, but startup watts were not published for a compressor, pump, or tool, or a published peak is above the motor-surge limit. A fan is marked surge risk only when its running watts are more than half the continuous output.

Won't run means the running watts are above continuous output and the load is not a simple heater that fits a documented resistive boost. Runtime is left blank in that case.

No run verdict means running watts were not published. An hour figure on those rows is only an energy budget from a published annual average. It is not a claim that the inverter can start the appliance.

## Runtime

Usable watt-hours are nameplate capacity times 0.85. That 0.85 is a Willrun allowance for inverter loss. It is not a measured efficiency for any model. The calculator, outage planners, brand comparison and CPAP/BiPAP pages add about 15 W of inverter self-consumption to the load.

Runtime is usable watt-hours divided by average draw. Average draw is the stored average when one exists, otherwise running watts times a duty cycle, otherwise the running watts themselves.

A combined calculator load uses the worst individual verdict. If the sum of running watts is above continuous output, and the loads are not all simple heaters inside a resistive boost, the mix will not run. Combined runtime uses the sum of average draws plus the 15 W inverter term.

## Duty cycle

A fridge duty cycle is stored only when the maker published both a wattage and an annual kWh figure. Average watts are annual kWh times 1,000 divided by 8,760. Duty cycle is that average divided by the published wattage. The label on those pages calls it an annual average, not a hot-day measurement.

Window air conditioners and dehumidifiers are not given a duty cycle. Their watt figures are the draw at the rated test condition. A sump pump has no duty cycle because how often the float runs depends on the inflow, which was not published.

## Derived watts

Window-unit running watts are Btu/h divided by the published CEER. That result matches the ENERGY STAR annual kWh figure at the DOE room-air-conditioner assumption of 750 hours, so it is used as rated cooling input. CEER is not a pure EER, and startup watts are still unpublished, so the verdict stays a surge risk.

Dehumidifier running watts come from pints per day times 0.473176 liters per pint, divided by 24 hours, divided by the integrated energy factor, times 1,000. That is the draw while the unit is removing water at the rated rate, not a whole-year average.

The Zoeller Model 53 running figure is 9.7 A times 115 V. The product page lists 4.8–9.7 A because the model is sold for 115 V and 230 V. The 9.7 A row is the 115 V automatic model in Zoeller's 50-series table.

## Surge, X-Boost, Power Lifting, and SurgePad

A published surge is used for motors only when the maker states it separately from a heater-only mode. X-Boost, Power Lifting, and SurgePad are stored as a resistive boost. They apply only when the appliance is a simple resistive heater and the element is between continuous output and that boost rating. Voltage can sag in that mode.

Microwaves and induction cooktops are electronics. They are not boost-eligible. A fan, a fridge, a window air conditioner, a dehumidifier, and a pump are not boost-eligible either.

EcoFlow's RIVER 2, RIVER 2 Max, RIVER 2 Pro, and RIVER 3 Plus publish a surge figure that is the same as X-Boost and is described for heating devices, so it is not used as motor-start capacity. The DELTA 2's 2,700 W surge appears on a 230 V manual line and is not used for the 120 V model. BLUETTI's AC180 lists a 2,700 W surge that the FAQ treats as Power Lifting and tells owners not to use for an air conditioner or a washer, so it is not used for motors. The AC70's 1,500 W surge is kept for motors; its 2,000 W lifting mode is resistive only. Anker's C300 headline surge matches the FAQ's SurgePad description, so it is a boost. The Goal Zero Yeti 1000X page disagrees with itself on surge (3,000 W and 3,500 W), so surge is omitted.

## What was left out

Specs that could not be read on a manufacturer page or an ENERGY STAR record were left blank or the model was dropped. Launch prices were not on the pages used, so every launch price is empty. Current shelf prices were not copied in.

Official pages for several smaller or newer stations did not resolve to a usable spec table, including Jackery Explorer 300 Plus, 600 Plus, and 500 v2, a Jackery 3000 Pro URL that opened a different product, and BLUETTI EB3A and Elite 200 V2 redirects. Those models are not in the set. The Anker F2000 marketing line of 3,600 W was not in the spec table, so it is not stored. A garbled DC voltage line on the DELTA Pro 3 page was omitted.

Common loads without a reputable running-watt source were omitted rather than filled from a generic watt chart: drip coffee makers, well pumps, corded power tools, oxygen concentrators, Starlink, garage-door openers, pellet stoves, box fans, kettles, toasters, slow cookers, rice cookers, hair dryers, air fryers, pressure cookers, electric blankets, and RV roof air conditioners. Full-size refrigerators and chest freezers in this set have ENERGY STAR annual kWh only, so they get no run verdict.

Laptop rows are an adapter maximum or an ENERGY STAR short-idle figure, not a measured full workload. Router watts are the TP-Link Archer AX73 networked-standby figure, not a marketing '3 W router' claim.

# Appliances

## Danby DCR032C1WDB 3.2 cu ft compact refrigerator

Page: https://willitrunpower.com/appliance/danby-dcr032c1wdb/
Category Refrigeration. Running 66.4 W. Peak not published W. Average 24.9 W. Duty cycle 0.375.
Source: https://www.danby.com/products/compact-refrigerators/dcr032c1wdb/
Danby lists 115 V, 66.4 W, and 218 kWh/year. Average draw is 218 × 1,000 ÷ 8,760 = 24.9 W. Duty cycle 0.375 is that average divided by 66.4 W, so it is an annual-average compressor fraction, not a hot-day measurement. Startup watts are not published.

## Lasko 755320 ceramic heater, high

Lasko lists 120 V, current 7.5 A to 12.5 A, and energy output 900 W to 1,500 W. High is 1,500 W. A resistive element does not have a separate motor surge, so surge is set equal to the high setting. The thermostat cycles in real rooms; this entry assumes the high element is on.

## Panasonic NN-SU656WAWH microwave, electrical input

Panasonic lists power supply 120 V / 60 Hz, microwave output 1,100 W, and microwave power consumption 1,500 W. The station has to supply the 1,500 W input, not the 1,100 W cooking output. A separate startup surge is not published. X-Boost and Power Lifting are not applied, because those modes are described for simple heating loads and a microwave is an electronic supply.

# EcoFlow vs Jackery vs BLUETTI (brand comparison, 2026-10-21)
URL: https://willitrunpower.com/guides/ecoflow-vs-jackery-vs-bluetti/
- Quick picks: under $400 small UPS = EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus ($299, 286 Wh, <10 ms, expands to 858 Wh). Cheapest 1 kWh in stock = Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 ($519 sale, list $589, 1,070 Wh, 23.8 lb, <20 ms). Bedside CPAP / grow-later 1 kWh = EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus ($719, list $799, <10 ms, 1,000 W solar, expands to 5 kWh). 2 kWh most capability for $899 = BLUETTI AC200L (2,048 Wh, 2,400 W, 7,200 W surge, 1,200 W solar, 20 ms UPS, expands to 8,192 Wh, 62.4 lb). Lightest 2 kWh = Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 ($899 sale, 39.5 lb, <20 ms, 400 W solar, not expandable). Solar-first 2 kWh = EcoFlow DELTA 2 Max ($1,049, 1,000 W solar, expands to 6,144 Wh, no published UPS time). Whole home / 240 V = EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 ($2,799, list $3,299, 4,096 Wh, 4,000 W 120/240 V, 2,600 W solar, 10 ms UPS, 12 kWh per unit).
- $/Wh at maker prices 2026-10-21: AC180 0.43, AC200L 0.44, Jackery 2000 v2 0.44, AC70 0.47 (sold out), Jackery 1000 v2 0.49, Jackery 1000 Plus 0.49, RIVER 2 Pro 0.51 (sold out), DELTA 2 Max 0.51, DELTA Pro 3 0.68, DELTA 3 Plus 0.70, RIVER 3 Plus 1.05.
- Runtime method: nameplate Wh x 0.85 / (load W + 15 W inverter draw). 100 W load: DELTA 3 Plus 7.6 h, Jackery 1000 v2 7.9 h, AC180 8.5 h, 2 kWh units about 15.1 h, DELTA Pro 3 30.3 h.
- Solar per 4.5 sun-hour day at max input (x0.75): Jackery v2 models 400 W = 1,350 Wh (about 66% of a 2000 v2); AC200L 1,200 W = 4,050 Wh; DELTA 2 Max / DELTA 3 Plus 1,000 W = 3,375 Wh; DELTA Pro 3 2,600 W = 8,775 Wh.
- Warranty: Jackery 3+2 years only from Jackery.com, Jackery-branded stores or authorized dealers (Amazon buyers register for the +2), refurbished 6 months; EcoFlow 5 years (DELTA Pro 3: 3 + 2 with app registration); BLUETTI 5 years. Cycle ratings: EcoFlow/BLUETTI to 80%, Jackery to 70%.
- Medical: Jackery says its stations are not recommended for medical devices; EcoFlow says not for life-sustaining equipment. Confirm with a doctor; commissions do not affect compatibility claims.

# Power station for an oxygen concentrator (outage guide, 2026-10-27)
URL: https://willitrunpower.com/best-power-station-for/oxygen-concentrator/
- Runtime on AC (h): Jackery 1000 v2 7.9 @100 W, 3.1 @275, 2.5 @350; DELTA 2 Max / Jackery 2000 Plus / AC200L 15.1, 6.0, 4.8; Anker F3800 28.4, 11.3, 8.9; DELTA Pro 3 30.3, 12.0, 9.5.
- Overnight (8 h) need: 100 W 1,082 Wh; 275 W 2,729 Wh; 325 W 3,200 Wh; 350 W 3,435 Wh. 24 h at 300-350 W is ~9-10 kWh, so batteries are a bridge, not a multi-day plan.
- Switchover: DELTA Pro 3 10 ms, Jackery 2000 Plus 20 ms EPS, Jackery 1000 v2 and Anker C1000 <20 ms. Perfecto2 V needs ~30 min warm-up to rated purity; Inogen At Home <5 min.
- Medical: general information only; Jackery says not recommended for medical devices, EcoFlow not for life-sustaining equipment; get non-electric backup cylinders from your supplier and register with your utility.

# Power station for an insulin fridge (outage guide, 2026-10-28)
